name: Planor HQ
tagline: A hosted HQ dashboard for running a small business or agency: clients, projects, and money in one place.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: All-in-one ops suites are wide, not deep: clients, projects, tasks, time, invoices, each one a CRUD table with a few joins and a PDF at the end. An agent will happily generate that in a sitting, and for a solo operator tracking their own work it will be enough. The gaps show up the moment other humans or other systems are involved: multi-user roles, an audit trail, email notifications, payment links, bank feeds, tax handling, and the boring invoice numbering rules your accountant cares about. This one is thinly documented publicly, so the verdict is on the category rather than on any specific feature depth. If you are one person who wants your own numbers in your own SQLite file, build it; if you are billing clients through it, buy something that has already been yelled at by an accountant.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app with clients, projects, tasks, tracked hours and invoices, where logged time rolls up into a PDF invoice you can send yourself.
requirements: a headless-Chrome or PDF library for invoice rendering
optional SMTP credentials in .env if you want to email invoices
whatYouLose: Multi-user accounts, roles and permissions, so anyone else touching it sees everything
Payment collection: no Stripe checkout links, no paid/unpaid reconciliation beyond a checkbox you tick
Accounting integrations and tax logic, VAT, sequential invoice numbers, exports your bookkeeper will accept
Mobile access, notifications and reminders for overdue invoices or stalled projects
Backups, uptime and the general reassurance that your business records exist somewhere other than one laptop
moatNotes: Ops suites win by being where the records already live. Once a year of invoices and client history is in there, migrating is a data-cleanup project nobody schedules.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value of a business HQ is not the forms, it is trusting that the records are correct, retrievable and shareable a year from now. Paid tools handle the parts you only notice when they break: invoice sequencing, tax fields, payment reconciliation, permissions for the contractor you just hired, and a backup you did not have to think about. A personal build is genuinely fine as a private dashboard and genuinely risky as your only source of truth for money.
notes: Wide-but-shallow suites are the easiest thing to clone and the hardest thing to trust with your invoices.
prompt:
Build a local-first business ops dashboard called "HQ" for a single freelancer or small agency. No cloud, no accounts, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- SQLite via better-sqlite3 with Drizzle ORM, one file at ./data/hq.db
- Server Actions for all mutations, no separate API layer
- Zod for input validation
- PDF invoices rendered with @react-pdf/renderer

Data model:
- clients: name, email, address, hourly_rate, notes, archived
- projects: client_id, name, status (lead, active, paused, done), budget_hours, notes
- tasks: project_id, title, status (todo, doing, done), due_date
- time_entries: project_id, task_id nullable, minutes, date, description, billed boolean
- invoices: client_id, number, issue_date, due_date, status (draft, sent, paid), line items as a child table, subtotal and total computed on save

Screens:
- Dashboard: unbilled hours by client, open invoice total, tasks due this week
- Clients list and detail with their projects and invoice history
- Project detail with tasks and a time log, plus hours-vs-budget bar
- Time tracker: quick entry form plus a start/stop timer stored in the DB, no browser-only state
- Invoices: create from unbilled time entries for one client, edit lines, mark sent or paid, download PDF, marking sent flips those time entries to billed

Rules:
- Invoice numbers are sequential per year, format YYYY-0001, never reused
- Money in integer cents, hours stored as minutes, no floats anywhere
- Seed script with two clients, three projects and a month of fake time entries
- npm run backup copies the SQLite file into ./backups with a timestamp
- .env holds only optional SMTP vars; the app must run fully with no .env present

Out of scope: auth, multi-user, Stripe, bank feeds, tax calculation, expense tracking, mobile app, email sending beyond an optional SMTP stub.

Deliver a README with setup, seed and backup commands, and make the whole thing run with npm install and npm run dev.
